facts.statement: The genus Unktaheela was described by Clark, O'Keefe, and Slack in 2023.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Clark, O'Keefe & Slack, 2023

facts.statement: Unktaheela is classified as an extinct genus of polycotylid plesiosaur.
facts.quote: Unktaheela is an extinct genus of polycotylid plesiosaur

facts.statement: Fossils of Unktaheela come from the Late Cretaceous Sharon Springs Formation in the United States.
facts.quote: from the Late Cretaceous Sharon Springs Formation of the United States

facts.statement: Unktaheela fossils were found in the Baculites obtusus zone of the Sharon Springs Formation in the United States.
facts.quote: The Unktaheela fossil material was discovered in sediments of the Sharon Springs Formation (Baculites obtusus zone) in the United States

facts.statement: The holotype specimen UCM 35059 was discovered near Redbird in Niobrara County, Wyoming.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, UCM 35059, was found near Redbird in Niobrara County, Wyoming

facts.statement: The paratype specimen SDSM 142501 was found on the Thomas Conger Ranch near Buffalo Gap in Fall River County, South Dakota.
facts.quote: The paratype specimen, SDSM 142501, was found on the Thomas Conger Ranch near Buffalo Gap in Fall River County, South Dakota

facts.statement: In 1996, Kenneth Carpenter initially identified the holotype specimen as a juvenile Dolichorhynchops osborni.
facts.quote: In 1996, Kenneth Carpenter described specimen UCM 35059 as belonging to a juvenile individual of the related Dolichorhynchops osborni

facts.statement: Robert O. Clark, F. Robin O'Keefe, and Sara E. Slack established Unktaheela specta as a new genus and species in 2023.
facts.quote: In 2023, Robert O. Clark, F. Robin O'Keefe, and Sara E. Slack described Unktaheela specta as a new genus and species of polycotylid based on these fossil remains

facts.statement: The name Unktaheela honors Unhcegila, a Lakota legend of a horned water serpent with keen eyes.
facts.quote: The generic name, "Unktaheela", references Unhcegila, a legendary Lakota horned water serpent known for its keen eyes

facts.statement: The species name specta refers to hypothesized visual adaptations linked to the large eye sockets.
facts.quote: The specific name "specta" is derived from the Latin word "spectare", meaning "to see," in reference to the hypothesized visual adaptations and morphology of the orbital

facts.statement: The genus Unktaheela contains only one known species, represented by two skulls and partial skeletons.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, U. , known from two skulls and partial skeletons

facts.statement: Unktaheela is the smallest known polycotylid plesiosaur.
facts.quote: Unktaheela represents the smallest known polycotylid

facts.statement: The holotype skull measures 44.4 cm in length, while the paratype skull is 43 cm long.
facts.quote: The holotype skull is 44.4 cm long, and the paratype skull is 43 cm long

facts.statement: Adult Unktaheela reached a total length of approximately 2.3 to 2.6 meters.
facts.quote: Unktaheela was approximately 2.3 - 2.6 m long

facts.statement: Unktaheela possessed at least 26 maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: Unktaheela had at least 26 maxillary teeth

facts.statement: Unktaheela skulls feature unusually large orbits, a trait often seen in juvenile animals.
facts.quote: The skull of Unktaheela has unusually large orbits, a feature commonly associated with juvenile animals

facts.statement: Many bones in Unktaheela specimens are fused, indicating they were fully grown despite juvenile-like skull features.
facts.quote: many bones are fused in the specimens that are typically unfused in juvenile plesiosaurs

facts.statement: Unktaheela had wide humeri, distinguishing them from the narrow humeri of juvenile plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: The humeri are wide, as opposed to the narrow form seen in juveniles

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Unktaheela within the plesiosaur clade Leptocleidia.
facts.quote: Clark, O'Keefe & Slack (2023) recovered Unktaheela as a polycotylid member of the plesiosaur clade Leptocleidia

facts.statement: Unktaheela, along with Dolichorhynchops species, forms the clade Dolichorhynchia within the Polycotylinae.
facts.quote: These species, together with Dolichorhynchops spp. (D. osborni and D. herschelensis), form the clade Dolichorhynchia within the Polycotylinae

facts.statement: Unktaheela lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Unktaheela's juvenile-like features represent true ontogeny or are unique adult characteristics.
facts.quote: Unktaheela was a very small polycotylid that, when mature, had some characteristics that might be expected of ontogenetically young individuals
